chain3.why: A–B first by score; B–C would join A and C

tie_by_pair_key.why: equal scores: pair key (A,B) < (B,C); pairs given reversed

judgment_first.why: the merge judgment C–D ranks above the 0.95 pair; B–C then joins B and D

refusal_cascade.why: B–C refused; C–D accepted; A–D refused because {A,B} and {C,D} hold A–C

two_cannots.why: B–C refused by A–C, A–D refused by B–D; in arrival order B–C first gives {A,D},{B,C}

duplicate_pair.why: A–B scored and judged counts once, as a judgment, so it precedes B–C at 0.99

isolated_and_long_chain.why: ties broken by pair key along the chain: E4–E5 is last and joins E1 and E5; X is cannot-linked only
